articleTitle: H2 Line Emission Associated with the Formation of the First Stars
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Molecular hydrogen (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm H}_2$</tex>) line radiation emitted in the formation events of first-generation stars is evaluated in a discussion of its detectability by future observational facilities. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm H}_2$</tex> luminosity evolution from the onset of prestellar collapse until the formation of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 100 \,{{{M}_{\odot}}}$</tex> protostar is followed. Calculations are extended not only to the early phase of the runaway collapse, but also to the later phase of accretion, whose observational features have not been studied before. Contrary to the runaway collapse phase, where the pure-rotational lines are always dominant, in the accretion phase rovibrational line emission becomes prominent. The maximum luminosity is also attained in the accretion phase for strong emission lines. The peak intensity of the strongest rovibrational line reaches <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 10^{-29} \,{\rm W} \,{\rm m}^{-2}$</tex>, corresponding to the flux density of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^{-5} \,\mu{\rm Jy}$</tex>, for a source at the typical redshift of first-generation star formation, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1+z = 20$</tex>. Although the redshifted rovibrational <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm H}_2$</tex> emission from such an epoch falls in the wavelength range of the next-generation infrared satellite, Space Infrared Telescope for Cosmology and Astrophysics, for exceeding the detection threshold, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^7$</tex> such protostars are required to reach the maximum luminosity simultaneously in a pregalactic cloud. It is improbable that this condition is satisfied in a realistic scenario of early structure formation.

articleTitle: Astronomical Observation with a Nb-Al-AlOX-Al-Nb STJ Single Photon Detecor for Optical Wavelengths
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: A test observation using a Nb-Al-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm AlO}_{X}$</tex>-Al-Nb superconducting tunnel junction detector was carried out using a small commercial optical telescope. Single photons of visible wavelengths were detected from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> Lyr, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> Boo, and Jupiter, and pulse-height distributions were obtained. The observed spectra roughly agree with predictions.

articleTitle: A Photometric Analysis and Spot Activity of BH Virginis
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: BH Virginis is a short-period eclipsing binary with two solar-type components. The photoelectric light curves in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$UBVRI$</tex>, observed by Scaltriti et al. (1985), and in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B$</tex> and 5125 Å bands, observed by Hoffmann (1982), were analyzed by using the 1992 version Wilson–Devinney program to investigate the activity of spots. The results show that there was a small cool spotted active region on the secondary star in 1984. The position and area of the active region in 1984 are remarkably similar to those in 1991. The distortion waves in the light curves observed by Hoffmann (1982) can be fitted satisfactorily with two hot-spot active regions: one is on the primary star, and the other is on the secondary component. The mass ratio <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q = m_{2} / m_{1}$</tex>, obtained from photoelectric light curves, is inside the range of 0.965–0.971. It is close to the spectroscopic value of 0.968 obtained by Zhai et al. (1990). To study the physical cause of the variations and the distortions in the light curve of BH Vir, the photoelectric observations in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$BV$</tex> observed by Koch (1967) were re-analyzed based on a new spot model with an assumption of one cool spot active region on the primary star and two cool spot active regions on the secondary star. The fit of the new spot model to the observations is better than that of our former result (Xiang et al. 2000). The present results suggest that BH Vir may have an active cycle with a period of 7–10 years.

articleTitle: An Ultrasoft Transient X-Ray Source near the Galactic Bulge Region
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Further analysis of an ultrasoft transient X-ray source near the Galactic bulge region is reported. This source was discovered in scanning observations with Ginga, and was at first designated as GS 1734<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>275 (Makino 1988). The source position was re-determined using revised satellite attitude data, and then this source was named GS 1732<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>273. The revised position is in agreement with those of the transient sources, KS 1732<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>273, discovered with Mir-Kvant in 1989, and 1RXS J173602.0<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>272541, discovered with the ROSAT all-sky survey in 1990. The X-ray spectrum, constructed by a scan-fit technique, is well represented by a multicolor disk model with a temperature at the inner disk radius of 0.7–0.8 keV. The spectral properties and the transient behavior suggest that GS 1732<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>273 is a candidate source of black hole binaries.

articleTitle: Optical Observation of the 2003 Outburst of a Black Hole X-Ray Binary, V4641 Sagittarii
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on the results of our optical photometric observations of a black hole X-ray binary, V4641 Sgr during an outburst in 2003 August. During the outburst, we detected several properties having noteworthy similarities to those observed during an outburst in 2002 May; the outburst lasted about 6 days, during which it exhibited flares and rapid fluctuations, having timescales of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^{2\hbox{-}4} \,{\rm s}$</tex>. In complicated profiles of light curves, we identified several recurring patterns, which were also observed during the 2002 outburst. First, the object frequently experienced sudden temporary fadings, which we call “dips”, appearing just after the states characterized by strong short-term fluctuations. Second, we detected optical flashes, which are characterized by a brightening by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 0.5 \,{\rm mag}$</tex> within <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 50 \,{\rm s}$</tex>. Based on the similarity of the outbursts in 2002 and 2003, we conclude that they have the same nature. This is the first time that repetitive outburst phenomena have been confirmed in V4641 Sgr. The object probably has an outburst interval that can be as small as 1–2 years.

articleTitle: Line-Profile Variations during an Eclipse of a Dwarf Nova, IP Pegasi
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Accretion disks are rotating disks formed by accreting matter onto compact objects, and are thought to be the source of various active phenomena. Dwarf novae, the best-studied disk systems, composed of a white dwarf with a surrounding disk and a red-dwarf companion star, exhibit double-peaked emission-line profiles because of disk rotation. When a disk is eclipsed by the companion star, the emission-line profiles vary with time, since a different portion of the disk having a different line-of-sight velocity is successively obscured. We report on spectacular variations of the line profiles during an eclipse that we obtained for the first time through Subaru spectroscopy of an eclipsing dwarf nova, IP Peg. Our fine data are useful for investigating detailed velocity profiles as well as the non-axisymmetric emissivity distribution. The observed variations are basically consistent with Keplerian rotation, but are more complex than those predicted by a simple axisymmetric model.

articleTitle: Global Structures of Optically Thin Black Hole Accretion Flows Obtained from Direct Magnetohydrodynamic Simulations
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We studied the global structures of radiatively inefficient black hole accretion flows by three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic simulations. The initial state is a constant angular-momentum torus threaded by weak toroidal magnetic fields. The torus is assumed to be embedded in a low-density, spherical, isothermal halo. We found that in the innermost region (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varpi < 15 \,r_g$</tex>: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r_g$</tex> is the Schwarzschild radius) of optically thin hot disks formed by accretion from the torus, the radial structure can be described by a one-dimensional steady transonic ADAF (Advection Dominated Accretion Flow) solution that takes into account the radial dependence of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex>. Numerical results indicate that the magnetic flux emerging from the disk creates a magnetically active layer in which magnetic reconnection generates outflows along magnetic field lines. We also studied the dependence of the disk structure on the external pressure of the initial torus. The saturation level of magnetic field amplification is higher for a model with a larger external pressure. Thus, external pressure enhances the magnetic activity of the disk. When the external pressure is 5–20% of the maximum pressure of the torus, the kinetic and Poynting energy flux of the outflow is about 1% of the energy flux advected to the black hole through accretion.

articleTitle: SDSS J1335+0118: A New Two-Image Gravitational Lens
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on the discovery of the two-image gravitationally lensed quasar SDSS J1335<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>0118. The object was selected as a lens candidate from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey. The imaging and spectroscopic follow-up observations confirm that the system exhibits two gravitationally lensed images of a quasar at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z = 1.57$</tex>. The image separation is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${1\rlap {.}{}^{\rm {\prime \prime }}56}$</tex>. We also detect an extended component between the two quasar images, likely to be a lensing galaxy. Preliminary mass modeling predicts a differential time delay, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta t$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim30 \, h^{-1} {\rm day}$</tex>, assuming the redshift of the lens galaxy to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.5$</tex>.

articleTitle: Formation of Opposite-Sign Magnetic Helicity by an Erupting Filament in a Coronal Mass Ejection
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: It is unclear whether it is possible for magnetic helical fields of opposite signs to co-exist in a coronal mass ejection (CME). During filament eruption with high-cadence observations for the initial stage, evidence is found for the formation of right-handed helical fields in a rising dextral filament that is embedded in a CME with helical fields in a left-handed sense. The data include Mees multi-off-band <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm H}\alpha$</tex> observations with 16 s cadence and TRACE 1600 Å observations of 2 s cadence. The filament material is ejected outward and is associated with the expanding CME, suggesting that both of the opposite-sign helical fields are injected into interplanetary space. In this paper, we consider the key observational features, including the formation of a coil-like structure (due to barb reconnections) and the alignment of reconnected field lines with the primary axis of the filament. It is found that they are consistent with the predicted changes during filament eruption by the filament model of Martin and McAllister. However, our results do not reject the filament model of Rust and Kumar. Moreover, a model that reconciles both of them seems to be more convenient for understanding the complicated observations. Therefore, the formation of opposite-sign helicity in an eruptive flux rope should be common for such types of filament eruptions.

articleTitle: Radiative Shocks in Rotating Accretion Flows around Black Holes
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: It is well known that rotating inviscid accretion flows with adequate injection parameters around black holes could form shock waves close to the black holes, after the flow passes through the outer sonic point and can be virtually stopped by the centrifugal force. We numerically examined such shock waves in 1D and 2D accretion flows, while taking account of the cooling and heating of the gas and the radiation transport. The numerical results show that the shock location shifts outward compared with that in adiabatic solutions, and that a more rarefied ambient density leads to a more outward shock location. In 2D-flow, we find an intermediate frequency QPO behavior of the shock location, as is observed in the black hole candidate GRS 1915<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>105.

articleTitle: 43 GHz SiO Masers and Astrometry with VERA in the Galactic Center
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present Very Large Array (VLA) observations of 43 GHz SiO (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J = 1 \hbox{-} 0, v = 2$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v = 1$</tex>) maser emission in a sub-sample of late-type stars in the Inner Galaxy selected on their relatively strong (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gt 0.5 \,{\rm Jy}$</tex>) 86 GHz SiO masers, and located within <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${2\rlap {.}{}^{\rm {\circ }}5}$</tex> of the galactic center. Furthermore we combine these results with a summary of previous surveys for 43 GHz SiO masers in the galactic center and comment on their use as calibrators for the Japanese “VLBI Exploration of Radio Astrometry” (VERA) network, which is intended to perform sub-milli-arcsecond astrometry in the Galaxy and the galactic center.

articleTitle: Cosmic Ray Acceleration at Ultrarelativistic Subshocks
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present a model of cosmic ray acceleration at ultrarelativistic subshocks, and confront it with observations of gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) and blazars. We consider cosmic ray acceleration in shocks with Lorentz factors (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex>) in the range 3–40. We show that fluctuations of the magnetic field downstream of the shock do not play an important role in the acceleration process; however, some fluctuations are needed to return a few per cent of the seed particles into upstream of the shock. The results of numerical simulations for shocks with considered Lorentz factors and perpendicular magnetic field inclinations are presented. We fit the derived particle energy spectral index (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma$</tex>) dependence on fluctuations of the magnetic field upstream and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex> with a function.

articleTitle: Detection of Short Fading Episodes in Two Dwarf Novae from VSNET Observations
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: From the observations reported to VSNET, we detected short fading episodes in two dwarf novae, RX And (orbital period 5.0 hr) and SU UMa (orbital period 1.8 hr). The episodes in RX And can be naturally explained as the response to a short-term reduction of the mass-transfer rate. A qualitative comparison with VY Scl-type fading is also discussed. In SU UMa, the same explanation is expected to be more difficult to apply. The viable, but still poorly understood, possibilities include a temporary reduction of the quiescent disk viscosity and a temporary reduction of the mass-transfer rate. If the latter possibility is confirmed, we probably need a different mechanism from that of VY Scl-type stars.

Author Keywords: stars: individual (RX Andromedae, SU Ursae Majoris)

articleTitle: Mass and Spin of GRS 1915 $+$ 105 Based on a Resonance Model of QPOs
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We demonstrate that the four high-frequency QPOs observed in GRS 1915<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>105 can be interpreted as the oscillation modes on disks that non-linearly and resonantly interact with a warp. The warp is assumed to be a low-frequency global pattern on the disk. This identification suggests that the relevant mass, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex>, and spin parameter, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a$</tex>, are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M = 13 \hbox{-} 14 \,{{{M}_{\odot}}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a = 0 \hbox{-} 0.15$</tex>.

articleTitle: Optical Variability of the Afterglow of GRB 030329
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on the optical light curve of the afterglow of GRB 030329. Our observation combined with publicly available data sets revealed that the light curve was rich in unexpectedly complicated structures throughout <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 6$</tex> days after the burst. Our early observation indicates that the light curve can be described by a single power-law model with bumps until a supernova component became dominant. The bumps superimposed on a fading trend had roughly constant amplitudes and colors. The long-lived, large-amplitude variations indicate that additional energy was supplied for the shock region. The refreshed shock scenario is most plausible. The observed slopes of the bumps during early times, however, contradict the prediction of this model.

articleTitle: VERA Observation of the W49NH2O Maser Outburst in 2003 October
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on a strong outburst of the W 49N <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm H}_2 {\rm O}$</tex> maser observed with VERA. Single-dish monitoring with VERA 20m telescopes detected a strong outburst of the maser feature at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\rm LSR} = -30.7 \,{\rm km} \,{\rm s}^{-1}$</tex> in 2003 October. The outburst had a duration of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 100$</tex> days and a peak intensity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$7.9 \times 10^4 \,{\rm Jy}$</tex>, being one of the strongest outbursts in W 49N observed so far. VLBI observations with the VERA array were also carried out near to the maximum phase of the outburst, and the outburst spot was identified in the VLBI map. While the map was in good agreement with previous studies, showing three major concentrations of maser spots, we found a newly formed arc-like structure in the central maser concentration, which may be a shock front powered by a forming star or a star cluster. The outburst spot was found to be located on the arc-like structure, indicating a possible connection of the present outburst to a shock phenomenon.

articleTitle: The Peculiar 2004 Superoutburst in the Helium Dwarf Nova, 2003aw
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We conducted a time-resolved photometric campaign of helium dwarf nova, 2003aw, in 2004 May–June. 2003aw stayed at 14.7–15.7 mag for the first several days during this campaign, which is the plateau phase of this superoutburst. This variable then rapidly decayed to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 18.0 \,{\rm mag}$</tex>, still brighter by about 2 mag than its quiescence magnitude, and maintained this brightness for about 20 days, having short flares of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 2 \,{\rm mag}$</tex>. A long fading tail followed it. We detected superhumps with a period of 0.02357(4)d [= 2036(3)s] during the plateau phase. The whole light curve of the superoutburst in 2003aw, taking into account the present data and those in the literature, perfectly resembles that of the 1996–1997 superoutburst of the peculiar WZ Sge-type hydrogen-rich dwarf nova, EG Cnc.

articleTitle: Discovery of a Peculiar Pulsar in the Small Magellanic Cloud
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on a peculiar X-ray binary pulsar, IKT 1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=$</tex> RX J0047.3<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>7312, observed with XMM-Newton in 2000 October. The X-ray spectrum is described by a two-component spectrum. The hard component has a broken power-law with respective photon indices of 0.2 and 1.8, below and above the break energy at 5.8 keV. The soft component can be modeled by a blackbody of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$kT = 0.6 \,{\rm keV}$</tex>. The X-ray flux shows a gradual decrease and periodic variations of about 4000 s. The averaged flux in 0.7–10.0 keV is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.9 \times 10^{-12} \,{\rm erg} \,{\rm cm}^{-2} \,{\rm s}^{-1}$</tex>, which is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 10$</tex>-times brighter than that in a ROSAT observation in 1999 November. In addition to the 4000-s variation, we found coherent pulsations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$263 \pm 1 \,{\rm s}$</tex>. These discoveries strengthen the Be/X-ray binary scenario proposed by the ROSAT and ASCA observations on this source, and confirm that most of the hard sources in the Small Magellanic Cloud are X-ray binary pulsars. A peculiar property of this XBP is that the coherent pulsations are found only in the soft component, and the folded light curve shows a flat top shape with a sharp dip. We discuss the nature of this XBP focusing on the peculiar soft component.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Magnetohydrodynamic Numerical Simulations of Coronal Loop Oscillations Associated with Flares
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We performed three-dimensional MHD numerical simulations for solar coronal magnetic loop oscillations and found: (1) The loop oscillation period is determined by its Alfvén time. (2) The amplitude of oscillation decreases exponentially in time. This is explained as energy transport by fast-mode MHD waves. The damping rate, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\omega _{\rm damp}$</tex>, is described as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\omega _{\rm damp} \propto V_{\rm a}/R$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\rm a}$</tex> is the Alfvén speed around loops and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex> is the radius of the loop. Because of computer resources limitations, the plasma <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex> value is much larger than that of the real corona. We thus applied a scaling law derived from numerical simulation results to the real corona parameter ranges and analyzed the results.

articleTitle: Unusual State in V Sagittae
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: It has recently been demonstrated that the recurring high/low states in the peculiar binary V Sge can be explained by considering limit-cycle oscillation involving negative feedback by the wind on the mass-transfer from the secondary star. We noticed, from recent observations reported to VSNET, the presence of a different state of recurring variations (recurrence time <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 30 \,{\rm d}$</tex>), showing a gradual rise and a sudden drop in brightness. The observed features of this light variation are unlikely to be reproduced by a limit-cycle oscillation mechanism involving a mass-transfer variation from the secondary star (Hachisu, Kato 2003). We suggest that this phenomenon originates from an unidentified intrinsic instability in the disk, or in the wind of a high-luminosity object, such as in V Sge.

articleTitle: Periods of Activity Cycle of Polar Faculae
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The periodicity of the high-latitude solar activity has been studied using monthly-averaged polar facula counts obtained at the National Astronomical Observatory of Japan (NAOJ) and the annual number of polar faculae observed by Mount Wilson Observatory (MWO). The complex Morlet wavelet was utilized to analyze the periodicity in the two data sets. For the NAOJ and MWO data, the most eminent period is 10.89 and 10.48 years, respectively, which is the Schwabe period of the high-latitude solar activity. All possible periods detected at the low-latitude solar activity were also detected in the two data sets, and we found no distinct periods existing just in the two data sets of the high-latitude solar activity. The periodicity of the high-latitude solar activity is inferred to be the same as that of the low-latitude solar activity.

articleTitle: A Deeply Eclipsing SU UMa-Type Dwarf Nova with the Shortest Orbital Period, XZ Eridani
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We discovered superhumps in an eclipsing dwarf nova, XZ Eridani, during an outburst in 2003 January–February. We determined the orbital and average superhump periods to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.061159602 \pm 0.000000044 \,{\rm d}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.062808\pm 0.000017 \,{\rm d}$</tex>, respectively. Our observations thus established that XZ Eri belongs to a rare class of deeply eclipsing SU UMa-type dwarf novae. The object has the shortest orbital period among seven known objects in this class. The superhump period decreased with time during a mid-plateau phase of the superoutburst, as observed in a number of ordinary, long-period SU UMa stars. During an early phase of the superoutburst, however, the superhump period increased, as observed in several short-period systems. XZ Eri is a unique object with which we can study the evolution of accretion-disk structures through eclipses during the phase of the superhump period increase.

articleTitle: Photometric Observations of an SU UMa-type Dwarf Nova, VW Coronae Borealis, during Outbursts
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on photometric observations of an SU UMa-type dwarf nova, VW CrB, during two superoutbursts in 2001 and 2003 and a normal outburst in 2003. Superhumps with a period of 0.07287(1) d were observed during the 2003 superoutburst. The change rate of the superhump period was positive. During a normal outburst, there is some hint of modulation up to a 0.2-mag amplitude. However, no periodicity was found. The recurrence cycles of the normal outburst and the superoutburst, and the distance were estimated to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ge 50 \,{\rm d}$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$270 \sim 500 \,{\rm d}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$690^{+230}_{-170} \,{\rm pc}$</tex>, respectively. These recurrence cycles are the usual values for an SU UMa-type dwarf nova having this superhump period. The superhump period of VW CrB was the longest among those of SU UMa stars with positive derivatives of the superhump period. The coverage of our observations was, however, not sufficient, and the variation of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P_{\rm SH}$</tex> change rate of VW CrB is still unknown. A superhump regrowth and a brightening were seen near the end of the plateau phase. Measuring the deviation of the start timings of the brightening and the superhump regrowth (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gt 2$</tex> days in VW CrB) will be a key to reveal the mechanism of these phenomena.

articleTitle: XMM-Newton Observations of G32.45+0.1 and G38.55+0.0: Diffuse Hard X-Ray Sources Found by the ASCA Galactic Plane Survey
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on XMM-Newton observations of G32.45<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>0.1 and G38.55<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>0.0. These were discovered as diffuse hard X-ray sources by the ASCA Galactic Plane Survey, but the limited spatial resolution of ASCA could not conclude whether these are truly diffuse or a group of unresolved point-sources. XMM-Newton, with higher spatial resolution than ASCA, confirmed that G32.45<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>0.1 has a diffuse shell-like structure with a radius of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim {4{}^{\rm {\prime }}}$</tex>. The spectrum shows a featureless continuum, and can thus be fitted by a power-law model of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma \sim 2.2$</tex> with an absorption of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N_{{\rm H}} \sim 5.2 \times 10^{22} \,{\rm cm}^{-2}$</tex>. From this <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N_{{\rm H}}$</tex> value, we estimated the distance to G32.45<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>0.1 to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 17 \,{\rm kpc}$</tex>. Thus, the luminosity (in the 0.5–10.0 keV band) and radius of the shell are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 9.5 \times 10^{34} \,{\rm ergs} \,{\rm s}^{-1}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 20 \,{\rm pc}$</tex>, respectively. The radio complex sources in the NRAO/VLA Sky Survey (NVSS; 1.4 GHz) are globally associated with the X-ray shell of G32.45<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>0.1. Therefore, G32.45<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>0.1 is likely to be a synchrotron-dominant shell-like SNR. No significant diffuse structure was found in the XMM-Newton image of another ASCA diffuse source, G38.55<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>0.0. The upper limit of the observed flux (0.5–10.0 keV) is estimated to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$9.0 \times 10^{-13} \,{\rm ergs} \,{\rm cm}^{-2} \,{\rm s}^{-1}$</tex>, which is consistent with the ASCA result.

articleTitle: X-Ray Expanding Features Associated with a Moreton Wave
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on the simultaneous observation of a Moreton wave in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm H}\alpha$</tex> and two kinds of coronal expanding features in soft X-rays near the solar limb. We consider the faster X-ray feature and the slower one as being an “X-ray wave” and “ejecta”, respectively. The chromospheric Moreton wave propagated on the solar disk at a speed of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1040 \pm 100 \,{\rm km} \,{\rm s}^{-1}$</tex>, whereas the coronal X-ray wave propagated outside of the disk toward the outer corona at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1400 \pm 250 \,{\rm km} \,{\rm s}^{-1}$</tex>. We identified the X-ray wave as MHD fast-mode shock. The fast-mode Mach number (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_{{\rm f}}$</tex>) of the X-ray wave was also estimated to be about 1.13–1.31, which decreases during propagation. The timing when the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_{{\rm f}}$</tex> became “1” is consistent with that of the disappearance of the Moreton wave. Moreover, we discuss the 3-dimensional structure of the shock wave and the relation between the shock wave and the ejecta (and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm H}\alpha$</tex> filament eruptions).

articleTitle: Partial Covering Interpretation of the X-Ray Spectrum of the NLS1 1H 0707−495
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The X-ray spectrum of 1H 0707<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>495 obtained with XMM-Newton showing a deep flux drop at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 7 \,{\rm keV}$</tex> (Boller et al. 2002) is studied based on the partial covering concept. The previously inferred extreme iron overabundance can be reduced down to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${}\sim 3\times$</tex> solar if the hard component gradually steepens at high energies. The spectral shape supports that 1H 0707<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>495 is an AGN analogue of the galactic black-hole binaries in the soft state. Interpreting the soft excess as the emission from an optically-thick disk, the minimum black hole mass <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> is estimated to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2 \cdot 10^6 \,{{{M}_{\odot}}}$</tex> from the intrinsic luminosity corrected for partial covering. Based on the slim disk model, the observed disk temperature implies that the luminosity is close to the Eddington limit. The rapid and large flux variations with little change in the spectral shape can also be explained, if not all, as due to changes in the partial covering fraction. Partial covering may account for the large variability characteristics of NLS1.

articleTitle: A Period Study of the Near-Contact Binary IR Cassiopeiae
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The near-contact binary IR Cas was observed in 2003 October. Two new observed times of the primary minimum were derived. All of the available eclipse times, including the new ones, spanning 90 years were analyzed. It was shown that the period change of the system is very complex. A period oscillation with a period of 53.24 years and an amplitude of about 0.0133 days were found, while it undergoes a secular decrease at a rate of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$dP/dt = -1.18 \times 10^{-7} (\pm0.09) \,{\rm d} \,{\rm yr}^{-1}$</tex>. The mechanisms that could explain the period changes and the evolutionary state of the system are discussed.

articleTitle: Reflection Component in the Hard X-Ray Emission from the Seyfert 2 Galaxy Mrk 1210
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The Seyfert 2 galaxy Mrk 1210 was found to exhibit a flat hard X-ray component by ASCA, although ASCA could not distinguish whether it is an absorbed direct component or a reflected one. We then observed Mrk 1210 with BeppoSAX, and found that the X-ray spectral properties are quite different from those of ASCA, as have been confirmed with XMM-Newton; the flux is significantly higher than that in the ASCA observation, and a clear absorption cut-off appears below 5 keV. A bright hard X-ray emission is detected up to 100 keV. The reflection component is necessary to describe the BeppoSAX PDS spectrum, and represents the ASCA hard component very well. Therefore, the hard component in the ASCA spectrum is a reflected one, whose intensity is almost constant over 6 yr. This indicates that a dramatic spectral variability is attributed to a large change of the absorption column density by a factor of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$>5$</tex>, rather than the variability of the nuclear emission. The change in the absorption column density means that the torus is not homogeneous, but has a blobby structure with a typical blob size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< 0.001 \,{\rm pc}$</tex>.

articleTitle: A Subaru Search for Lyman$\alpha$Emitters atz = 5.8 with an Intermediate-Band Filter
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present the results of a survey for Ly<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex>emitters at<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z \approx 5.8$</tex>using a new intermediate-band filter centered at<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{\rm c} \approx 8275</tex> Å with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta\lambda_{\rm FWHM} \approx 340</tex> Å (i.e., spectroscopic resolution is<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R \approx 24$</tex>) and a combination with a traditional narrow-band centered at<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{\rm c} \approx 8150</tex> Å with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta\lambda_{\rm FWHM} \approx 120</tex> Å (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R \approx 68$</tex>). Our observations were made using the Subaru Prime Focus Camera, Suprime-Cam, on the 8.2m Subaru telescope in a sky area surrounding the high-redshift quasar SDSSp J104433.04<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>012522.2 at<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z = 5.74$</tex>, covering an effective sky area of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\approx 720 \;{\rm arcmin}^2$</tex>. In this survey, we have found four Ly<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex>-emitter candidates from the intermediate-band image (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z \approx 5.8$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta z \approx 0.3$</tex>). Combined with our previous results based on theNB816imaging, we discuss the star-formation activity in galaxies between<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z \approx 5.7$</tex>and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z \approx 5.9$</tex>.

articleTitle: On the Period Variation of the Neglected W UMa-type Binary System V714 Monocerotis
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Some new CCD times of the light minimum for a neglected W UMa-type binary star, V714 Monocerotis, observed in 2002 and 2003, are presented. By considering the general trend of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm O}- {\rm C}$</tex> variation, a plausible <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm O}- {\rm C}$</tex> curve was formed and a mean linear ephemeris was obtained. It was found that the period of the binary star shows a continuous decrease with rate of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$dP/dt = -1.48 \times 10^{-7} \;{\rm d} \;{\rm yr}^{-1}$</tex>. In order to understand the evolutionary state of the binary system, new photometric and spectroscopic observations and a careful investigation on those data are required.

articleTitle: Soft X-Ray Transients as Ultraluminous X-Ray Sources
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We discuss the possibility that the soft X-ray transient GRS 1915<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>105 evolved from a binary similar to V4641 Sgr (XTE J1819<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-$</tex>254) by conservative mass-transfer, and estimate the possible mass-transfer rates during the evolution. The results indicate that the high mass-transfer rates could explain the high luminosities in ultraluminous X-ray sources. Although the high mass-transfer rates during evolution are accompanied by high luminosities, we find that much of the transferred matter may sweeps accompanying radiation in an adiabatic inflow of super-Eddington accretion. We suggest that soft X-ray transients with evolved companions (initial companion mass <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gt 3 \,{{{M}_{\odot}}}$</tex>), e.g. GRS 1915<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>105, can be ultraluminous X-ray sources if they are seen through their beaming axis.

articleTitle: Nucleosynthesis inside an Accretion Disk in a Type II Collapsar
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Taking into account the increasing mass of a central object through fall-back, we investigated nucleosynthesis inside an accretion disk formed during a core collapse of a massive star. It has been confirmed that the disk is an advection-dominated accretion flow supported by gas or radiation pressure. A sequence of (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha, \gamma$</tex>) reactions take place and Fe-group elements are produced inside the disk. At the early phase of the fall-back, when O-rich materials inflow, the ejected gas contains abundant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{54\atop} {\rm Fe}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{56, 58\atop} {\rm Ni}}$</tex>. At the late phase the in-coming material is He-rich and the out-going gas is abundant of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{44\atop} {\rm Ti}}$</tex> as well as Fe and Ni. Provided that the processed gas outflows from the inner region up to the ejection radius, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r_{\rm ej}$</tex>, we find that the ejected mass of the heavy elements is not very sensitive to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r_{\rm ej}$</tex>, as long as we take <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r_{\rm ej} \ge 50 \,r_{\rm g}$</tex>, because these elements are produced mainly in the region <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20 \hbox{-} 100 \,r_{\rm g}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Of NBOs and kHz QPOs: a Low-Frequency Modulation in Resonant Oscillations of Relativistic Accretion Disks
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The origin of quasi periodic modulations of flux in the kilohertz range (kHz QPOs), observed in low-mass X-ray binaries, is usually assumed to be physically distinct from that of the “normal branch oscillations” (NBOs) in the Z-sources. We show that a low-frequency modulation of the kHz QPOs is a natural consequence of the non-linear relativistic resonance suggested previously to explain the properties of the high-frequency twin peaks. The theoretical results discussed here are reminiscent of the 6 Hz variations of frequency and amplitude of the kHz QPOs reported by Yu, van der Klis, and Jonker (, ApJ, 559, L29).

articleTitle: First mm-VLBI Observations between the TRAO 14-m and the NRO 45-m Telescopes: Observations of 86 GHz SiO Masers in VY Canis Majoris
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We have made VLBI observations at 86 GHz using a 1000-km baseline between Korea and Japan with successful detections of SiO <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v = 1, J = 2$</tex> -<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex> maser emissions from VY CMa and Orion KL in 2001 June. This was the first VLBI result for this baseline and the first astronomical VLBI observation for the Korean telescope. Since then, we observed SiO <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v = 1, J = 2$</tex> -<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1$</tex> maser emission in VY CMa in 2002 January and 2003 February and derived the distributions of the maser emissions. Our results show that the maser emissions extend over 2–4 stellar radii, and were within the inner radius of the dust shell. We observed other SiO maser sources and continuum sources, and 86-GHz continuum emissions were detected from three continuum sources. It was verified that this baseline has a performance comparable to the most sensitive baseline in the VLBA and the CMVA, and is capable of investigating the proper motions of maser features in circumstellar envelopes using monitoring observations.

articleTitle: General Relativity and the Pseudo-Newtonian Potential
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We propose a metric correction on velocities calculated from the Paczyński and Wiita (1980) pseudo-Newtonian potential, in order to avoid the divergence to infinity at the Schwarzschild radius. Cold disk flows onto a black hole are briefly discussed.

articleTitle: The Anisotropic Transfer of Resonance Photons in Hot Plasmas on Magnetized White Dwarfs
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: In order to confirm the anisotropic effect of resonance photons in hot accretion columns on white dwarfs in magnetic cataclysmic variables, proposed by Terada et al. (2001), systematic studies with ASCA of 7 polars and 12 intermediate polars were performed. The equivalent widths of He-like Fe <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm K}\alpha$</tex> lines of polars were found to be systematically modulated at their spin periods in such a way that it increases at the pole-on phase. This implies that the anisotropic mechanism is commonly operating among polars. On the other hand, those of intermediate polars are statistically consistent with being unmodulated with an upper limit of 1.5-times modulation. This may be due to a different accretion manner, like an aurora curtain (Rosen et al. 1988), so that the plasma also becomes optically thin along the horizontal axis for the resonance lines, or because of larger optical depths for Compton scattering if the emission regions have the same coin-like shapes as polars.

articleTitle: A Modified Hermite Integrator for Planetary Dynamics
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We describe a modified time-symmetric Hermite integrator specialized for the long-term integration of planetary orbits. Our time-symmetric integrators have no secular errors in the semimajor axis and the eccentricity for the integration of two-body Kepler problems as usual time-symmetric and symplectic integrators. The usual time-symmetric or symplectic integrators, however, show a secular drift in the argument of pericenter. Our new family of integrators has one free parameter, which we can adjust to reduce the error in the argument of pericenter without breaking the time-symmetry or changing the order of the integrator. We show analytically that the leading term of the error vanishes for a unique value of the parameter, which is independent of the size of the timestep and the eccentricity. It is also possible to eliminate the non-leading, higher-order terms by using a parameter value that depends on both the size of the timestep and the eccentricity. We describe the second- and the fourth-order schemes. An extension to higher order is straightforward.

articleTitle: Importance of Prolate Neutrino Radiation in Core-Collapse Supernovae: The Reason for the Prolate Geometry of SN1987A?
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We have carried out 2-D simulations of core-collapse supernova explosions. The local neutrino radiation field was assumed to have its maximum value either at the symmetry (polar) axis or on the equatorial plane. These led to prolate and oblate explosions, respectively. We have found that the gain of the explosion energy in the prolate explosion evolves more predominately than that in the oblate one when the total neutrino luminosity is given. Namely, the prolate explosion is more energetic than the oblate one.One of the authors (Shimizu et al. 2001) showed for the first time that globally anisotropic neutrino radiation produces a more powerful explosion than does spherical neutrino radiation. In our previous study (Madokoro et al. 2003), we improved the numerical code of Shimizu et al. (2001), and demonstrated that globally anisotropic neutrino radiation yields a more energetic explosion than does spatially-fluctuated neutrino radiation. Together with the result of this paper, we conclude that globally anisotropic (prolate) neutrino radiation is the most effective way to increase the explosion energy among various types of explosions investigated in these studies. We discuss the reason for this. Our result is suggestive of the fact that the expanding materials of SN1987A have been observed to have a prolate geometry.

articleTitle: Near-Infrared Unidentified-Line Morphology of the Planetary Nebula NGC 7027
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Medium-resolution (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R \sim 500$</tex>), <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>-band two-dimensional spectra are presented for the planetary nebula NGC 7027. The spatial distributions for the two bright unidentified lines near 2.199 and 2.287<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\, {\mu \rm {m}}$</tex> were revealed and examined compared to those of other emission lines. It was spatially confirmed that the unidentified lines do not arise from neutral molecules, but ionized species. The ionization potentials of their parent ions are lower than that of He II, and comparable to or higher than that of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Br}\gamma$</tex>. Our results support the previous studies of identification of parent species, on the condition that the carriers of the unidentified lines are partly excited by collisions.

articleTitle: Twin Peaks kHz QPOs: Mathematics of the 3:2 Orbital Resonance
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Using the method of multiple scales, one can derive an analytic solution that describes the behaviour of weakly coupled, non-linear oscillations in nearly Keplerian discs around neutron stars or black holes close to the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3:2$</tex> orbital epicyclic resonance. The obtained solution agrees with a previous numerical simulation. Such a result may be relevant to the kilohertz quasi-periodic variability in X-ray fluxes observed in many Galactic black hole and neutron star sources. With a particular choice of tunable parameters, the solution fits accurately the observational data for Sco X-1.

articleTitle: $\Delta T$ and the Tidal Acceleration of the Lunar Motion from Eclipses Observed at Plural Sites
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: An eclipse on 188 BC July 17 was observed and recorded both at Chang’an (China) and Rome (Italy). An eclipse on AD 873 July 28 was observed and recorded both at Nishapur (Iran) and Kyoto (Japan). The eclipse was annular at Nishapur. These plural records of deep eclipses are rare in history, and are useful for determining the clock correction, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta T$</tex>, and the lunar tidal acceleration, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\dot{n}$</tex>. We have tried to determine as precisely as possible the ranges of these two parameters. If we fix the tidal acceleration to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$- {25\rlap {.}{}^{\rm {\prime \prime }}83} \,{\rm cy}^{-2}$</tex>, we get, as a best estimate, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$12581 \,{\rm s} < \Delta T < 12741 \,{\rm s}$</tex> from the 188 BC eclipse and contemporary eclipses, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3327 \,{\rm s} < \Delta T < 3498 \,{\rm s}$</tex> from the AD 873 eclipse and contemporary eclipses.

articleTitle: 2:3 Twin Quasi-Periodic Oscillations in Magnetohydrodynamic Accretion Flows
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract:
We have studied the radial and vertical oscillations in three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) accretion flows around black holes. General-relativistic effects were taken into account by using a pseudo-Newtonian potential. We found that the structure of MHD flows is changed at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.8 \,r_{{m s}} \leq r \leq 6.3 \,r_{{m s}}$</tex>, and that two pairs of quasi-periodic oscillations (twin QPOs) are excited in that region. The time evolution of the power spectrum density (PSD) indicates that these twin QPOs are most likely to be produced by a resonance between the Keplerian frequency, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$
u_{m K}$</tex>, and the epicyclic frequency, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$
u_{\kappa}$</tex>. The PSD shows that the lower peak frequency, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$
u_{m l}$</tex>, corresponds to, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$
u_{m K}$</tex>, while the upper peak frequency, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$
u_{m u}$</tex>, corresponds to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$
u_{m K} + 
u_{\kappa}$</tex>. The ratio of two peak frequencies is close to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2:3$</tex>. The results provide the first direct evidence for the excitation of resonant disk oscillation in MHD accretion flows.

articleTitle: Probing Warm-Hot Intergalactic Medium Associated with the Virgo Cluster Using an Oxygen Absorption Line
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: To detect a warm-hot intergalactic medium (WHIM) associated with the large-scale structure of the universe, we observed a quasar behind the Virgo cluster with XMM-Newton. With 54 ks exposure, we marginally detected an O VIII <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm K}\alpha$</tex> absorption line at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$650.9^{+0.8}_{-1.9} \,{\rm eV}$</tex> in the RGS spectra, with a statistical confidence of 96.4%. The observed line center energy is consistent with the redshift of M 87, and hence the absorber is associated with the Virgo cluster. From the curve of growth, the O VIII column density was estimated to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gtrsim 7 \times 10^{16} \,{\rm cm}^{-2}$</tex>. In the EPIC spectra, excess emission was found after evaluating the hot ICM in the Virgo cluster and various background components. We inspected the RASS map of the diffuse soft X-ray background, and confirmed that the level of the north and west regions just outside of the Virgo cluster is consistent with the background model that we used, while that of the east side is significantly higher and the enhancement is comparable with the excess emission found in the EPIC data. We consider a significant portion of the excess emission to be associated with the Virgo cluster, although a possible contribution from the North Polar Spur cannot be excluded. Using the column density and the emission measure and assuming an oxygen abundance of 0.1 and an ionization fraction of 0.4, we estimate that the mean electron density and the line-of-sight distance of the warm-hot gas are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lesssim 6 \times 10^{-5} \,{\rm cm}^{-3}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gtrsim 9 \,{\rm Mpc}$</tex>. These strongly suggest detection of a WHIM in a filament associated with the Virgo cluster.

articleTitle: On the Possibility of V4444 Sgr as a Recurrent Nova
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: V4444 Sgr (Nova Sgr 1999) has recently been suggested to be a possible recurrent nova based on the detection of preexisting dust, which may have been formed in a previous outburst. We examined this possibility using the available outburst observations, including the VSNET observations. We also noticed that this nova was recorded in the OGLE II public photometric database, which covered both preoutburst and late-decline phases. The outburst light curve constructed from these observations showed a plateau phase, particularly in the OGLE II <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I$</tex>-band light curve, which was followed by a more rapid decline. The light curve resembled those of “fast” recurrent novae and candidates in the presence of the distinct plateau phase. The outburst spectrum and the preoutburst magnitude more resemble those of classical novae, but they do not exclude the possibility of a recurrent nova.

articleTitle: Sound Speed and the Pseudo-Newtonian Potential
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We propose a special-relativistic correction to the sound speed calculated from the (Paczyński and Wiita 1980) pseudo-Newtonian potential, in order to avoid divergence to infinity at the Schwarzschild radius. Under this correction, the re-scaled sound speed approaches <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c/\sqrt{3}$</tex> at the Schwarzschild radius; otherwise, it diverges there. Spherical flows onto a black hole are briefly discussed.

articleTitle: Offsets between Hα and CO Arms of a Spiral Galaxy, NGC 4254: A New Method for Determining the Pattern Speed of Spiral Galaxies
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We examined the offsets between H II regions and molecular clouds belonging to spiral arms of a late-type spiral galaxy, NGC 4254 (M99). We used a high-resolution <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{12\atop} {\rm CO}}$</tex> (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J = 1 \hbox{-} 0$</tex>) image obtained by Nobeyama Millimeter Array (NMA) and an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm H}\alpha$</tex> image. We derived angular offsets (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta$</tex>) in the galactic disk, and found that they show a linear dependence on the angular rotation velocity of the gas (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega_{{\rm G}}$</tex>). This linear relation can be expressed by the equation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta = (\Omega_{{\rm G}}-\Omega_{{\rm P}}) \cdot t_{{\rm H}\alpha}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega_{{\rm P}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t_{\rm H\alpha}$</tex> are constant. Here, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega_{{\rm P}}$</tex> corresponds to the pattern speed of the spiral arms and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t_{{\rm H}\alpha}$</tex> is interpreted as being the timescale between the peak compression of the molecular gas in the spiral arms and the peak of massive star formation. We could thus determine <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega_{{\rm P}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t_{{\rm H}\alpha}$</tex> simultaneously by fitting a line to our <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta \hbox{-} \Omega_{{\rm G}}$</tex> plot, if we assume they are constant. From the plot for NGC4254, we obtained <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t_{{\rm H}\alpha} = (4.8 \pm 1.2) \times 10^6 \,{\rm yr}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega_{{\rm P}} = 26^{+10}_{-6} \,{\rm km} \,{\rm s}^{-1} \,{\rm kpc}^{-1}$</tex>, which are consistent with previous studies. We suggest that this <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta \hbox{-} \Omega_{{\rm G}}$</tex> plot can be a new tool to determine the pattern speed and the typical timescale needed for star formations.

articleTitle: 1993 Superoutburst of LL Andromedae
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present time-resolved CCD photometry of LL And during its 1993 outburst. The observation revealed the presence of superhumps with a period of 0.05697(3)d. This period is one of the smallest among the hydrogen-rich dwarf novae. Although LL And has been proposed to be a WZ Sge-type dwarf nova based on its low outburst frequency, our new analysis indicates that the outburst amplitude (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 5 \,{\rm mag}$</tex>) and outburst duration (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$9\pm 2 \,{\rm d}$</tex>) are much smaller and shorter than in typical WZ Sge-type dwarf novae. We suspect that the unusual outburst properties of LL And might be explained by assuming a “leaky disk” in quiescence, which was originally proposed to explain the prototypical WZ Sge-type outbursts. By combining with the recent suggestion of the orbital period, the fractional superhump excess is found to be 3.5(1)%, which is unusually large for this short-period system. LL And may be an object filling the gap in the evolutionary track, which has recently been proposed to explain the unusual ultracompact binaries with an evolved mass donor.

articleTitle: Inversion Formula for Determining the Parameters of an Astrometric Binary
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: It is believed that some numerical technique must be employed for determining the system parameters of a visual binary or a star with a planet, because the relevant equations are not only highly nonlinear, but also transcendental owing to Kepler’s equation. Such common sense, however, is not true; we have discovered an analytic inversion formula, in which the original orbital parameters are expressed as elementary functions of the observable quantities, such as the location of four observed points and the time interval between these points. The key thing is that we use the time interval, but not the time of each observation, in order to avoid treating Kepler’s equation. The present formula can be applied even in cases where the observations cover a short arc of the orbit during less than one period. Thus, the formula will be useful in future astrometric missions, such as SIM, GAIA, and JASMINE.

articleTitle: V1494 Aql: Eclipsing Fast Nova with an Unusual Orbital Light Curve
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present the time-resolved photometry of V1494 Aql (Nova Aql 1999 No. 2) between 2001 November and 2003 June. The object is confirmed to be an eclipsing nova with a period of 0.1346138(2) d. The eclipses were present in all observed epochs. The orbital light curve shows a rather unusual profile, consisting of a bump-like feature at phase 0.6–0.7 and a dip-like feature at phase 0.2–0.4. These features were probably persistently present in all available observations between 2001 and 2003. A period analysis outside of the eclipses has confirmed that these variations have a period common to the orbital period, and are unlikely to be interpreted as superhumps. We suspect that the structure (probably in the accretion disk) fixed in the binary rotational frame is somehow responsible for this feature.

articleTitle: Galaxy Structures and External Perturbations in Gravitational Lenses
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: In modeling strong gravitational lens systems, one often adopts simple models, such as singular isothermal elliptical density plus lowest-order external perturbation. However, such simple models may mislead us if the real mass distribution is more complicated than that in the assumed models. In particular, assumptions on mass models are crucial in studying flux ratio anomalies that have been suggested as evidence for a cold dark-matter substructure. We reinvestigated four quadruple lens systems using power-law Fourier models, which have advantages of clear physical meanings and the applicability of a linear method, as well as a simple singular isothermal elliptical density model. We also investigated the effect of external perturbations, including a singular isothermal sphere, lowest-order expansion, and next-order expansion. We have found that the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\cos 3\theta$</tex> terms of the primary galaxy and/or of external perturbation significantly reduce the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\chi^2$</tex> in PG 1115<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>080 and B1422<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>231. In particular, we could reproduce the flux ratios of B1422<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>231 with next-order external perturbation assuming 5% flux uncertainties, suggesting that external perturbation cannot be described by a simple singular isothermal sphere approximation. On the other hand, we could not fit B0712<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>472 and B2045<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+$</tex>265 very well even with our models, although the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\chi^2$</tex> were reduced compared with the case of using simple models. Our results clearly demonstrate that both the primary lens galaxy and the external perturbation are often more complicated than we usually assume.

articleTitle: A Shape-and-Density Model of the Putative Binary EKBO 2001QG298
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Recent observations of the Edgeworth-Kuiper belt object (EKBO) 2001 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm QG}_{298}$</tex> (Sheppard, Jewitt 2004) have shown that the lightcurve of this object has a very large amplitude (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.14 \pm 0.04 \,{\rm mag}$</tex>), indicating that it is either of an elongated shape or of a binary structure with two components of similar sizes nearly in contact with each other. On the basis of these interesting published data, we employed Roche binary lightcurve simulations to construct a shape model of EKBO 2001 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm QG}_{298}$</tex>. The shape parameters of the best-fitted model were <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$260\ (164) \times 205 (130) \times 185\ (116) \,{\rm km}$</tex> for the primary, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$265 (168)\times 160\ (102) \times 150\ (94) \,{\rm km}$</tex> for the secondary in the case of an albedo of 0.04 (0.10). An additional result of this calculation is that the average bulk density of the contact binary system could be estimated to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$630 \,{\rm kg} \,{\rm m}^{-3}$</tex>. This value is similar to that of several icy moons of Saturn with a diameter of less than 200 km. We have also used the Jacobi ellipsoidal approximation to compute the shape of one of the largest EKBOs, Varuna. The corresponding shape parameters are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a : b : c = 1.00 : 0.76 : 0.50$</tex>. The lower limit of the bulk density is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rho \ge 1000 \,{\rm kg} \,{\rm m}^{-3}$</tex>. These results are in good agreement with the published values of Jewitt and Sheppard (2002), and are consistent with their suggestion that larger icy bodies have higher densities (Sheppard, Jewitt 2002).

articleTitle: Radio Observations of the Afterglow of GRB 030329
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present results of the radio observations of the afterglow of GRB 030329 with the Nobeyama 45-m telescope. The observations were made at 23.5 GHz, 43 GHz, and 90 GHz. The light curves show a steep decline after a constant phase. The start time of the decline depends on the frequency. Namely, the decline started earlier at a higher frequency. The spectrum has a peak in the mm wavelength range. The peak frequency and the peak flux decreased with time. These results are consistent with the expectation from the fireball model.

articleTitle: Chandra Observation of Luminous Sources in the Nearby Irregular Galaxy NGC 4449
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Using archival Chandra ACIS-S data, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.5 \hbox{-} 8.0 \,{\rm keV}$</tex> X-ray spectra of two luminous X-ray sources in the nearby dwarf irregular galaxy NGC 4449 were studied. One, with an extremely high luminosity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.3 \times 10^{39} \;{\rm erg} \,{\rm s}^{-1}$</tex> in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.5 \hbox{-} 8.0 \;{\rm keV}$</tex> band, shows a spectrum that is well described with a power-law model of photon index <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 2$</tex>. Its properties are consistent with those of ultraluminous compact X-ray sources observed in nearby galaxies. The spectrum of the other, with a luminosity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.7 \times 10^{38} \,{\rm erg} \,{\rm s}^{-1}$</tex> in the same band, is successfully represented with a so-called multi-color disk blackbody emission model with an inner-most disk temperature of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 0.59 \,{\rm keV}$</tex>. Its spectral parameters are typical of ordinary black hole binaries observed in our Galaxy and the Large Magellanic Cloud. These young population objects, together with a bright supernova remnant and diffuse hot gas already reported, suggest that the X-ray emission from irregular galaxies is generally enhanced by their recent star-forming activities.

articleTitle: A High-Resolution Very Large Array Observation of a Protostar in OMC-3: Shock-Induced X-Ray Emission by a Protostellar Jet
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Using the Very Large Array (VLA) in the A-configuration, we obtained a high-resolution 3.6 cm map of a hard X-ray source detected by the Chandra X-ray Observatory in a protostellar clump in Orion molecular cloud 3.
